requirements.text: The system will interface with the bar-code reader to interface all transaction details.
The system will interface with the thumb-print reader for verifying claims form used by the clients.
The voucher numbers are system generated and created with unique identification numbers with security protocols in-built.
The system shall provide a validity date check for the period of vouchers to be used in the program.
The system shall allow authorized users to amend or alter the validity date of the voucher.
The system shall provide a provision to with-hold any voucher number if the admin team decides to do for any reason.
The system shall automatically generate a Distribution Invoice No.
The system shall automatically change the status of a VSP to In-activate if more than two fraud entries are found during the claim process.
The system shall automatically generate the Claim number with Hospital Code as Suffix + 8 digit.
The system shall automatically make a count on thumb impression mismatches for the same patient on the same voucher.
The system shall automatically In-Activate the VSP if the claim from the same VSP has more than two times of thumb impression mismatching.
The system shall save the user information only if the Password and Verify password values are equal.
The system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) and audit logging for all sensitive transactions, ensuring compliance with industry-standard encryption for data at rest and in transit.
The system shall enforce a password policy requiring a minimum of 12 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and special characters.
Voucher numbers shall be generated using a cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) to prevent enumeration or prediction of valid vouchers.
The system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) and audit logging for all sensitive data modifications, compliant with ISO/IEC 27001 standards.
The database shall maintain query response times under 2 seconds for standard reports and undergo automated index maintenance weekly to prevent fragmentation.
The system shall flag claims for manual review if the claim amount exceeds the provider's historical average by 20% or if mandatory fields are missing.
The system shall support a data entry throughput of at least 10 claims per minute per user, with a screen response time of less than 200ms for all field validations.
The database shall maintain query response times of under 1 second for all standard reports with a dataset size of up to 100,000 records.

OPEN: The PRD mentions biometric thumb-print verification but lacks requirements for secure storage and protection of biometric data. - Biometric data shall be stored as non-reversible cryptographic hashes, and the system shall comply with applicable data protection regulations regarding sensitive health and biometric information.

OPEN: The system lacks a defined backup and disaster recovery strategy for critical voucher and claim data. - The system shall perform automated daily incremental backups and weekly full backups, with a recovery time objective (RTO) of 4 hours.

OPEN: The system mentions a pilot of 20,000 vouchers but lacks long-term growth projections or maximum concurrent user capacity. - The system shall support a concurrent user load of 50 users and a database capacity of at least 1,000,000 records without performance degradation.
